verdict.reasoning: Patient reports 'soreness in my fingers' and 'the skin on my hands is kind of cracked'; doctor clarifies 'mainly the palm' and asks about itchiness, to which patient replies 'yeah, it does get itchy.' Duration is 'A couple of months ago. Like, three, four months ago.'

When asked why she came today, patient says, 'it's gotten to a point where it hurts a lot, and I can't really do my job,' and she works 'as a housekeeper.' This indicates recent worsening and interference with work.

Patient notes, 'I have dryness, like, you know, in other parts, like my legs, but it's not... very... It's not severe... it's just a little bit of dryness in my legs.' This supports mild leg dryness.

In review of systems, doctor asks about 'fever or temperatures, any nausea or any vomiting?'; patient answers 'No.' Doctor also asks, 'Any problem with your bowels?' and 'Any problems with your urine?' and patient answers 'No' to each.

Doctor asks, 'Any skin problems? Eczema, dermatitis, for example?' Patient replies, 'Not that I know of. No, I haven't been diagnosed.'
When asked about other conditions, patient states, 'I have diabetes.'
In medication history, patient answers, 'Metformin.' to 'Which medication do you take?'
Doctor asks, 'Do you have any allergies either to any medications or in general?' but the transcript provides no patient response. A claim of 'no known allergies' is not documented.
For family history, patient answers 'Diabetes as well?' and confirms 'Yes.'

Patient says, 'I do work as a housekeeper' and later specifies her workplace is 'a hotel.' She also states, 'I'm not always very good about wearing gloves,' and confirms using cleaning products (e.g., 'I usually use bugs for bathrooms').
Doctor asks, 'Do you smoke at all?' Patient answers, 'No.'
On alcohol, patient says 'Once a week. A couple of pints. A week?' and doctor summarizes 'so very minimal alcohol there.'
The transcript contains no physical examination maneuvers or vital signs; the entire encounter is history and counseling, so stating that none are documented is consistent.

Doctor states, 'I think you might have something called dermatitis or contact dermatitis,' linking it to 'people in your field who are using cleaning products, not using gloves.' This is based on sore, cracked, itchy palms, occupational exposure, and poor response to E45 and antihistamines.

Diabetes is noted ('I have diabetes') and metformin use, but there is no explicit assessment that diabetes is 'stable' or commentary on control, so this is adding interpretation not in the transcript.

Doctor advises, 'I strongly recommend that you wear gloves when cleaning at all times.' While 'laundry' is not mentioned, the core advice to wear gloves for cleaning is documented; inclusion of laundry slightly extends but does not contradict.
Doctor says, 'we can try some steroid creams to help with inflammation,' which indicates a prescribed topical steroid.
Doctor plans 'some stronger emollients which you really need to kind of coat on throughout the day, three, four times a day for the next couple of weeks.'
In response to patient's question about medicines, doctor says, 'So I'll do a prescription for you now and send over to your pharmacy.'

Doctor advises, 'If it still hasn't got better in about a week to two weeks time, I really want you to come back and see me again,' and clarifies 'a minimum couple of weeks, 10 days to 14 days,' and to return sooner if 'it's getting worse, if it's spreading or dryness is getting worse.'
